newsitem.title: UK: Unichem sees full year profits up eight pct.
newsitem.headline: Unichem sees full year profits up eight pct.

text.p: British drug wholesaler Unichem Plc said on Monday it expected full-year pretax profits, excluding the costs of its bid for Lloyds Chemists Plc, to rise eight percent to more than 53.5 million pounds.

The company said in a statement that fully diluted earnings per share, before bid costs, would rise six percent to more than 20.2p and the final net dividend would total 5.8p per share, giving a total 8.8p for the year.
The company said the estimated results reflected further growth in sales and profits from every division. Group sales were expected to rise by five percent.
The company said British wholesaling sales were expected to have risen by five percent, with second-half growth of eight percent and flat operating margins.
The forecasts refer to the year ended December 31, 1996.
In the retail pharmacy division, sales were expected to have risen by 18 percent with a "material" increase in operating margins, Unichem said in the statement.
Unichem's statement came after its German rival Gehe AG raised its bid for Lloyds last Friday in a move that analysts predicted would be the knock-out blow in their year-long bidding battle.
